title: A Protocol for Shielding-Enhanced Loading of Single Polar Molecules into Optical Tweezers
authors: Reuben R. W. Wang, Christian H. Nunez, Conner Williams, Amanda Younes, Li Du, Hossein R. Sadeghpour, Kang-Kuen Ni
abstract: We propose the high-fidelity preparation of single bosonic molecules in optical tweezers starting from small tweezer-trapped molecular ensembles. Our scheme combines a static electric field and a microwave field to generate strong, tunable, anisotropic interactions that shield the molecules against two-body collisional loss. We show that this shielding eliminates all long-range bound states, preventing three-body recombination. This elimination persists for all microwave ellipticities, including the experimentally practical limit of linear polarization. Application of an additional electric field gradient can be used to induce controlled spilling of strongly interacting molecules out of the trap until one remains. With realistic experimental parameters, we estimate that single tweezer-trapped NaCs molecules can be isolated from a pair with fidelities exceeding 99\%, and $> 95\%$ per site across an array. These results establish collisional shielding with electric fields as an effective tool for preparing highly-filled tweezer arrays of polar molecules.
summary: This paper proposes a novel, high-fidelity protocol to load single polar molecules into arrays of optical tweezers. It achieves this by using a combination of static and microwave electric fields to induce 'collisional shielding,' which suppresses detrimental molecular loss. The technique is highly relevant for creating controllable, highly-filled quantum simulators using dipolar quantum matter.
main_problem: The primary challenge is achieving high-fidelity preparation of single bosonic molecules within optical tweezer arrays while suppressing molecular loss mechanisms.
main_result: The proposed protocol, utilizing combined static and microwave electric fields for 'collisional shielding,' enables the isolation of single molecules with estimated fidelities exceeding 99% per site.
method:
The method combines theoretical modeling of molecular interactions with a proposed experimental protocol involving field application ($\vec{E}_{dc}$ and $\vec{E}_{ac}$) and controlled potential gradient application ($

model_or_system: The system involves polar molecules (e.g., NaCs) trapped in optical tweezers. The physics is modeled using a dressed rigid rotor Hamiltonian, incorporating dipole-dipole interactions derived from both first- and second-order perturbation theory.
key_observables: Loading fidelity, two-body and three-body loss rates ($\Gamma_{	ext{loss}}$), and the single-molecule occupancy probability $P_1(t)$.
important_parameters: Static electric field strength ($E_{dc} \approx 2.366 	ext{ kV/cm}$), microwave Rabi frequency ($\Omega$), and the detuning ratio ($\delta = \Delta/\Omega$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the ability to create initial molecular ensembles and models the loss process using Fermi's golden rule, approximating complex integrals with simplified forms.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the entire protocol, showing the setup with external fields, the mechanism of shielding enforcing repulsive interactions, and the final step where a field gradient induces controlled tunneling to achieve single-molecule loading.
paper_structure: The paper develops the theoretical framework by first defining the Hamiltonian and deriving the effective potential ($V_{eff}$). It then details the shielding mechanism, followed by the application of a field gradient to induce controlled single-molecule loading, and finally, it analyzes loss rates and occupancy probabilities.
why_interesting: This work provides a detailed, quantitative roadmap for controlling complex, interacting quantum many-body systems (polar molecules) in optical lattices, which is central to quantum simulation and quantum information processing.
